races.paceDynamic: Laravie is the sole confirmed pace-setter in a three-runner field over 1m6f on Good to Firm ground at Yarmouth, and with no rival willing to push for the lead, she will dictate every yard of this race at a tempo entirely of her own choosing. Coming off a hat-trick of wins over similar trips on Good ground and carrying the momentum of six-from-recent form, Laravie is likely to bowl along at a comfortable, sustainable gallop that never truly tests the field's stamina reserves until late. Betelgeuse and Captain Brett are both hold-up types who will have no choice but to settle in behind and wait for a signal to challenge, meaning the race becomes a late procession unless Laravie is collared in the final furlong. This race shape overwhelmingly favours horses who can track a single uncontested leader and produce a clean, well-timed finish — a profile that suits hold-up horses who have the racing style to close on a solo front-runner, but equally rewards a front-runner who dictates and isn't asked to quicken hard.

With only three runners, any incident at the start — a slow break or early interference — would immediately reshape the entire tactical picture, as even a length's advantage at the first bend becomes significant over this trip.

races.paceDynamic: Rocking Ends is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner 5f sprint on Good to Firm ground at Yarmouth, and with no genuine rival to press him early, he should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset. Havana Blast will look to sit just off the pace in a prominent position, while the hold-up contingent of Twilight Calls, Michaela's Boy, Law Of Average, and Cressida Wildes will be forced to work from behind — though Law Of Average and Cressida Wildes are true hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear of the field is over-subscribed with closers who cannot all find a clear run in a small field. A single front-runner setting a measured pace on a flat, fast track with no pressure is a scenario that historically suits hold-up horses who can sprint through from off the pace — but with four closers competing for the same finishing surge and Rocking Ends controlling fractions, the race shape most clearly favours horses with tactical versatility near the pace or strong finishing ability from a prominent pitch. The directional verdict is that Rocking Ends' uncontested lead sets up a pace scenario that rewards prominent racers and strong finishers equally, but the compressed, uncontested gallop slightly favours those who can travel smoothly in the first two positions rather than those buried in a traffic-laden hold-up group.

watchPoints.text: Rocking Ends sets the entire race shape — watch whether Jack Mitchell allows him to stride on from the gates or is checked into a false rhythm by any early jostling from Havana Blast, as the tempo he sets in the first two furlongs determines every subsequent scenario.

Law Of Average and Cressida Wildes are both genuine hold-up horses operating in an over-populated closing group of four — watch for traffic and crowding issues in the straight as Joey Haynes and Connor Planas look for daylight simultaneously on a five-furlong track with no room to manoeuvre around horses.

Twilight Calls is on a six-day turnaround after a recent run, which is a short recovery window for an eight-year-old sprinter — watch the paddock for any signs of freshness or fatigue before concluding the quick return is straightforward.

Havana Blast's headgear and his natural prominently-raced style make him the most tactically well-placed of the non-front-runners — watch whether Daniel Muscutt can secure the position directly behind Rocking Ends from the gates, as that slot is the most coveted in this race shape.

Good to Firm is confirmed for this race on the going report despite the stated GOOD in the race header — all pace and going assessments should reflect the faster surface, which marginally favours hold-up horses with a sharp turn of foot over pure front-running stamina.

Sea Suite and Cancan In The Rain are the most credible prominent types capable of sitting just off the pace, while Red Hat Eagle also prefers to race with cover from the front.
